Model Formula: MAP = DBP + (SBP − DBP)/3 = (SBP + 2 × DBP)/3
Model Reasoning: At initial admission, before treatment, blood pressure was 110/70 mmHg. These units are equivalent to mm Hg, so no conversion is required. Using the standard mean arterial pressure approximation: pulse pressure = 110 − 70 = 40 mm Hg; MAP = 70 + 40/3 = 83.333... mm Hg, rounded to 83.33. The later post-treatment blood pressure of 75/40 mm Hg is excluded.

Model Formula: BMI = weight (kg) / [height (m)]²
Model Reasoning: At admission, weight was 68 kg and height was 182 cm. Convert height: 182 cm ÷ 100 = 1.82 m. Square height: 1.82² = 3.3124 m². Calculate BMI: 68 ÷ 3.3124 = 20.5289 kg/m², rounded to 20.53 kg/m².

Model Formula: Cockcroft–Gault: CrCl (mL/min) = [(140 − age in years) × weight in kg] / [72 × serum creatinine in mg/dL], with a factor of 0.85 for females only. BMI = weight (kg) / height (m)^2. Devine ideal body weight for males = 50 + 2.3 × (height in inches − 60) kg. For overweight patients, adjusted body weight = ideal body weight + 0.4 × (actual weight − ideal body weight).
Model Reasoning: Use the initial preoperative creatinine of 1.39 mg/dL, not measurements or renal status after surgery. Convert height: 175 cm ÷ 100 = 1.75 m; 175 cm ÷ 2.54 = 68.8976 inches. Weight is already in kg and creatinine is already in mg/dL, so neither requires conversion. BMI = 87 ÷ 1.75² = 28.4082 kg/m², indicating overweight; therefore use adjusted body weight. Ideal body weight = 50 + 2.3 × (68.8976 − 60) = 70.4646 kg. Adjusted body weight = 70.4646 + 0.4 × (87 − 70.4646) = 77.0787 kg. For this male patient, CrCl = [(140 − 53) × 77.0787] ÷ (72 × 1.39) = 6705.8504 ÷ 100.08 = 67.0041 mL/min. Calculations retain unrounded intermediate values.

Model Formula: Corrected calcium (mg/dL) = measured calcium (mg/dL) + 0.8 × [normal albumin (g/dL) − measured albumin (g/dL)].
Model Reasoning: Using the admission values before treatment: calcium is 8.4 mg/dL (no conversion needed), and albumin is 33 g/L = 3.3 g/dL. The albumin deficit is 4 − 3.3 = 0.7 g/dL. The calcium correction is 0.8 × 0.7 = 0.56 mg/dL. Corrected calcium = 8.4 + 0.56 = 8.96 mg/dL.

Calculator Name: CKD-EPI Equations for Glomerular Filtration Rate

Model Inputs.unit_conversion: Creatinine is already in the required units: 1.7 mg/dL × 1 = 1.7 mg/dL. Age is already in years.

Model Formula: 2021 CKD-EPI Creatinine equation: eGFR = 142 × min(Scr/κ, 1)^α × max(Scr/κ, 1)^(-1.200) × 0.9938^Age × 1.012 (if female), where Scr is in mg/dL; κ = 0.9 and α = -0.302 for males. eGFR is expressed in mL/min/1.73 m².
Model Reasoning: Use the pretreatment admission creatinine of 1.7 mg/dL and age 81. Scr/κ = 1.7/0.9 = 1.888889. Thus min(1.888889, 1)^(-0.302) = 1, and max(1.888889, 1)^(-1.200) ≈ 0.4662. The age factor is 0.9938^81 ≈ 0.6043. The female multiplier does not apply. Therefore eGFR = 142 × 1 × (1.7/0.9)^(-1.200) × 0.9938^81 = 39.9999 mL/min/1.73 m², rounded to 40.0.

Model Formula: Devine formula for men: ideal body weight (kg) = 50 + 2.3 × [height (inches) − 60].
Model Reasoning: Use the admission height before treatment. Convert height using 1 inch = 2.54 cm: 173 ÷ 2.54 = 68.11023622 inches. Height above 60 inches = 8.11023622 inches. Ideal body weight = 50 + (2.3 × 8.11023622) = 68.65354331 kg, rounded to 68.65 kg. Actual body weight is not used in the Devine formula.

Model Formula: Bazett formula: QTc = QT / sqrt(RR), with QT and RR in seconds.
Model Reasoning: Using the initial measurements, convert QT: 330 msec / 1000 = 0.330 seconds. Calculate RR: 60 seconds/minute / 113 beats/minute = 0.5309734513 seconds. Then QTc = 0.330 / sqrt(0.5309734513) = 0.452874155 seconds. Convert to msec: 0.452874155 × 1000 = 452.874155 msec, rounded to 452.87.

Model Inputs.race: Not specified; Black race multiplier not applied

Model Formula: IDMS-traceable four-variable MDRD equation: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m²) = 175 × [serum creatinine (mg/dL)]^(-1.154) × [age (years)]^(-0.203) × 0.742 if female × 1.212 if Black.
Model Reasoning: Use the admission creatinine before treatment. Creatinine is already in the required units: 1.36 mg/dL × 1 = 1.36 mg/dL; age is already in years. Apply the female coefficient of 0.742. Black race is not documented, so no race multiplier is applied. Substitution gives 175 × 1.36^(-1.154) × 85^(-0.203) × 0.742 = 175 × 0.70129 × 0.40582 × 0.742 = approximately 36.95 mL/min/1.73 m².

Model Formula: FIB-4 = (age [years] × AST [U/L]) / (platelet count [10^9/L] × √ALT [U/L]).
Model Reasoning: Use the initial, pretreatment values. AST 107 IU/L and ALT 104 IU/L are numerically equivalent to 107 U/L and 104 U/L. Convert platelets: 181,000 cells/µL × 10^6 µL/L = 181 × 10^9 cells/L. The numerator is 35 × 107 = 3,745. The denominator is 181 × √104 = 181 × 10.198039 = 1,845.845. Thus, FIB-4 = 3,745 / 1,845.845 = 2.028881, rounded to 2.03.

Model Inputs.unit_conversion: Weight is already in kilograms; no conversion is required.

Model Formula: Holliday–Segar hourly maintenance fluid estimate (4–2–1 rule): 4 mL/kg/hr for the first 10 kg + 2 mL/kg/hr for the next 10 kg + 1 mL/kg/hr for each kilogram above 20 kg.
Model Reasoning: Using the pretreatment admission weight of 76 kg: first 10 kg × 4 mL/kg/hr = 40 mL/hr; next 10 kg × 2 mL/kg/hr = 20 mL/hr; remaining (76 − 20) = 56 kg × 1 mL/kg/hr = 56 mL/hr. Total = 40 + 20 + 56 = 116 mL/hr. This is a weight-based maintenance estimate, not a resuscitation-fluid prescription.

Model Inputs.unit_conversions: None required: admission sodium is in mEq/L and glucose is in mg/dL.

Model Formula: Hillier (1999): Corrected sodium (mEq/L) = measured sodium (mEq/L) + 2.4 × [(glucose (mg/dL) − 100) / 100].
Model Reasoning: Using the initial, pretreatment measurements: glucose excess = 350 − 100 = 250 mg/dL. Sodium correction = 2.4 × (250 / 100) = 6.0 mEq/L. Corrected sodium = 132 + 6.0 = 138 mEq/L.

Model Inputs.sodium: 136.4 mEq/L at admission; for monovalent sodium, 136.4 mEq/L = 136.4 mmol/L
Model Inputs.BUN: 11 mg/dL at admission; 11 ÷ 2.8 = 3.929 mmol/L of urea
Model Inputs.alcohol: 0 mg/dL as specified; 0 ÷ 4.6 = 0 mmol/L of ethanol

Model Formula: Calculated serum osmolality (mOsm/kg) = 2 × sodium (mEq/L) + glucose (mg/dL)/18 + BUN (mg/dL)/2.8 + ethanol (mg/dL)/4.6.
Model Reasoning: Using only pretreatment admission values: 2 × 136.4 = 272.8; 125/18 = 6.944; 11/2.8 = 3.929; 0/4.6 = 0. Total = 272.8 + 6.944 + 3.929 + 0 = 283.673 mOsm/kg, rounded to 283.67. This is calculated osmolality; measured osmolality may be higher because ingested ethylene glycol is not included in this standard formula.

Model Inputs.total_bilirubin: 36.1 mg/dL at admission; already in the required units
Model Inputs.serum_creatinine: 7.78 mg/dL at admission; already in the required units; capped at 4.0 mg/dL for calculation
Model Inputs.serum_sodium: 133 mEq/L at admission = 133 mmol/L because sodium is monovalent
Model Inputs.dialysis: Not receiving dialysis at initial presentation; subsequent hemodialysis is excluded

Model Formula: UNOS/OPTN MELD-Na: MELD = 10 × [0.957 × ln(creatinine) + 0.378 × ln(total bilirubin) + 1.120 × ln(INR) + 0.643]. Creatinine and bilirubin are in mg/dL; each laboratory input is floored at 1.0, and creatinine is capped at 4.0 mg/dL. Round MELD to the nearest integer and constrain it to 6–40. For MELD > 11, MELD-Na = MELD + 1.32 × (137 − Na) − 0.033 × MELD × (137 − Na), with Na constrained to 125–137 mmol/L. Round the final score to the nearest integer and constrain it to 6–40.
Model Reasoning: Use admission values, not baseline creatinine or later dialysis status. The creatinine input is min(7.78, 4.0) = 4.0 mg/dL. MELD = 9.57 × ln(4.0) + 3.78 × ln(36.1) + 11.2 × ln(2.2) + 6.43 = 13.267 + 13.556 + 8.831 + 6.430 = 42.084. After rounding and applying the upper limit, MELD = 40. Sodium 133 is within the permitted range, so 137 − 133 = 4. MELD-Na = 40 + 1.32 × 4 − 0.033 × 40 × 4 = 40 + 5.28 − 5.28 = 40.

Calculator Name: HOMA-IR (Homeostatic Model Assessment for Insulin Resistance)
Model Formula: Standard HOMA1-IR = fasting insulin (mIU/L) × fasting glucose (mmol/L) / 22.5; equivalently, fasting insulin (μIU/mL) × fasting glucose (mg/dL) / 405.
Model Reasoning: Use the admission fasting glucose and immunoreactive insulin measured before insulin therapy. HOMA-IR = (14.5 × 298) / 405 = 4321 / 405 = 10.6691, rounded to 10.67.

Model Formula: Free water deficit = total body water × [(measured serum sodium / desired serum sodium) − 1]; total body water ≈ 0.5 × body weight for a female.
Model Reasoning: Use the initial sodium and weight, excluding later measurements. Sodium is monovalent, so 126 mmol/L = 126 mEq/L. Estimated total body water = 0.5 × 35 = 17.5 L. Free water deficit = 17.5 × [(126/140) − 1] = 17.5 × (−0.1) = −1.75 L. Using water density ≈ 1 kg/L, this equals −1.75 kg. The negative result indicates an estimated free water excess rather than a deficit.

Model Formula: Anion gap (mEq/L) = serum Na⁺ − (serum Cl⁻ + serum HCO₃⁻), using the standard formula excluding potassium.
Model Reasoning: All inputs are from the initial, pretreatment serum chemistry measurements. The reported units, meq/l, are equivalent to mEq/L, so no numerical conversion is required. Use serum bicarbonate 9.4 mEq/L rather than the separate arterial blood gas bicarbonate. Chloride + bicarbonate = 118 + 9.4 = 127.4 mEq/L. Anion gap = 140 − 127.4 = 12.6 mEq/L.

Model Formula: Friedewald formula: LDL-C (mg/dL) = total cholesterol (mg/dL) − HDL-C (mg/dL) − triglycerides (mg/dL)/5.
Model Reasoning: All admission lipid values are already in mg/dL, so no unit conversion is needed. Triglycerides are below 400 mg/dL, permitting use of the standard Friedewald estimate, although fasting status is not specified. Estimated VLDL-C = 95/5 = 19 mg/dL. LDL-C = 161 − 39 − 19 = 103 mg/dL.

Model Formula: FENa (%) = (urine sodium × serum creatinine) / (serum sodium × urine creatinine) × 100
Model Reasoning: For monovalent sodium, 1 mEq/L equals 1 mmol/L. Creatinine values are converted from mg/dL to mg/L by multiplying by 10. Substituting the admission values: FENa = (12.0 × 15.6) / (197 × 1281) × 100 = 187.2 / 252357 × 100 = 0.0741806%, rounded to 0.0742%.

Model Formula: Framingham formula: QTc = QT + 0.154 × (1 − RR), with QT, QTc, and RR in seconds.
Model Reasoning: Use the initial values: heart rate = 87 bpm and QT = 405 msec. Convert QT: 405 / 1000 = 0.405 sec. Calculate RR: 60 / 87 = 0.6896551724 sec. Then QTc = 0.405 + 0.154 × (1 − 0.6896551724) = 0.4527931034 sec. Convert to msec: 0.4527931034 × 1000 = 452.7931034 msec, rounded to 452.79 msec.

Calculator Name: Framingham Risk Score for Hard Coronary Heart Disease
Model Formula: NCEP ATP III Framingham point-based score for 10-year hard coronary heart disease (MI or coronary death) in men: total points = age points + age-specific total cholesterol points + HDL cholesterol points + systolic blood pressure/treatment points + age-specific smoking points. Convert total points to risk using the published men's risk table.
Model Reasoning: Use the initial examination values before statin treatment. Age is already in years, cholesterol values are already in mg/dL, and blood pressure is already in mmHg, so no unit conversions are required. Age 79 (75–79 years) contributes 13 points. Total cholesterol 190 mg/dL (160–199 at age 70–79) contributes 1 point. HDL cholesterol 49 mg/dL (40–49) contributes 1 point. Untreated systolic blood pressure 120 mmHg (120–129) contributes 1 point; aspirin is not antihypertensive treatment. Nonsmoking contributes 0 points. Total = 13 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 0 = 16 points. The published men's table maps 16 points to a 25% 10-year risk. Family history, LDL cholesterol, BMI, and physical activity are not direct inputs to this scoring table.

Model Formula: Fridericia formula: QTc = QT / RR^(1/3), with QT and RR in seconds; multiply QTc by 1000 to convert to msec.
Model Reasoning: Using the initial presentation values: QT = 373 msec ÷ 1000 = 0.373 seconds. RR = 60 seconds/min ÷ 161 beats/min = 0.3726708075 seconds. QTc = 0.373 / (0.3726708075)^(1/3) = 0.518322872 seconds. Converting to msec: 0.518322872 × 1000 = 518.322872 msec, rounded to 518.32 msec.

Model Formula: Mosteller formula: BSA (m²) = √[(height (cm) × weight (kg))/3600].
Model Reasoning: At initial presentation, height was 180 cm and weight was 85 kg. These are already in the required units, so no conversion is needed. BSA = √[(180 × 85)/3600] = √(15300/3600) = √4.25 = 2.06155 m², rounded to 2.06 m².

Model Formula: Hodges formula: QTc (msec) = QT (msec) + 1.75 × [heart rate (bpm) − 60].
Model Reasoning: The initial heart rate is 101 bpm and QT interval is 280 msec. Both are already in the required units; 280 msec = 0.280 seconds, so no conversion is needed for this formula. QTc = 280 + 1.75 × (101 − 60) = 280 + 1.75 × 41 = 280 + 71.75 = 351.75 msec.

Model Formula: Rautaharju formula: QTc = QT × (120 + HR) / 180, where HR is in beats/min and QTc has the same units as QT.
Model Reasoning: Using the initial values, convert QT: 321 msec ÷ 1000 = 0.321 seconds. QTc = 0.321 × (120 + 68) / 180 = 0.321 × 188 / 180 = 0.3352667 seconds. Convert to msec: 0.3352667 × 1000 = 335.2667 msec, rounded to 335.27 msec.

Model Formula: BMI = weight (kg) / [height (m)]²; therefore, target weight (kg) = target BMI × [height (m)]².
Model Reasoning: Convert height: 72 in × 0.0254 m/in = 1.8288 m. Square height: (1.8288 m)² = 3.34450944 m². Calculate target weight: 23.2 kg/m² × 3.34450944 m² = 77.592619008 kg, rounded to 77.59 kg.

Model Formula: Adjusted body weight (kg) = IBW + 0.4 × (actual body weight − IBW), using the Devine formula for women: IBW (kg) = 45.5 + 2.3 × (height in inches − 60).
Model Reasoning: Use the admission weight of 78 kg, not the historical 40 kg weight loss. Convert height: 160 cm ÷ 2.54 cm/inch = 62.9921259843 inches. Ideal body weight = 45.5 + 2.3 × (62.9921259843 − 60) = 52.3818897639 kg. Adjusted body weight = 52.3818897639 + 0.4 × (78 − 52.3818897639) = 62.6291338583 kg, rounded to 62.63 kg.

Model Formula: Delta gap = (anion gap − 12) − (24 − HCO3), where anion gap = Na − (Cl + HCO3).
Model Reasoning: Use admission values before bicarbonate administration or haemodialysis. Sodium, chloride, and bicarbonate are monovalent, so mmol/L equals mEq/L. Anion gap = 142 − (123 + 14) = 5 mEq/L. Increase in anion gap = 5 − 12 = −7 mEq/L. Decrease in bicarbonate = 24 − 14 = 10 mEq/L. Delta gap = −7 − 10 = −17 mEq/L.

Model Formula: Delta ratio = (anion gap − 12)/(24 − HCO3−), where anion gap = Na+ − (Cl− + HCO3−), excluding potassium.
Model Reasoning: Use the initial admission laboratory values, before correction of acidosis. All electrolyte concentrations are already in mEq/L, so no unit conversion is needed. Anion gap = 148 − (117 + 8.6) = 22.4 mEq/L. Increase in anion gap = 22.4 − 12 = 10.4 mEq/L. Decrease in bicarbonate = 24 − 8.6 = 15.4 mEq/L. Delta ratio = 10.4/15.4 = 0.6753, rounded to 0.68; units cancel.

Model Formula: Albumin-corrected anion gap = [Na − (Cl + HCO3)] + 2.5 × (4.0 − albumin), with electrolytes in mEq/L and albumin in g/dL (standard albumin correction; potassium excluded).
Model Reasoning: All patient inputs are from initial admission before treatment. Electrolytes are already in mEq/L and albumin is already in g/dL, so no unit conversions are required. Uncorrected anion gap = 127 − (101 + 9) = 17 mEq/L. Albumin correction = 2.5 × (4.0 − 1.8) = 5.5 mEq/L. Corrected anion gap = 17 + 5.5 = 22.5 mEq/L.

Model Formula: Anion gap (AG) = Na − (Cl + HCO3). Albumin-corrected AG = AG + 2.5 × (4.0 − albumin in g/dL). Albumin-corrected delta gap = (albumin-corrected AG − 12) − (24 − HCO3).
Model Reasoning: Only pretreatment admission measurements are used. Electrolytes are already in mEq/L and albumin is already in g/dL, so no unit conversions are required. The albumin correction factor is 2.5 mEq/L per g/dL. AG = 143 − (120 + 12.5) = 10.5 mEq/L. Albumin correction = 2.5 × (4.0 − 2.1) = 4.75 mEq/L. Corrected AG = 10.5 + 4.75 = 15.25 mEq/L. The increase in corrected AG is 15.25 − 12 = 3.25 mEq/L; the bicarbonate deficit is 24 − 12.5 = 11.5 mEq/L. Therefore, the albumin-corrected delta gap = 3.25 − 11.5 = −8.25 mEq/L.

Model Inputs.admission_bicarbonate: 7.5, interpreted as mEq/L because the note omits its unit

Model Formula: AG = Na − (Cl + HCO3); albumin-corrected AG = AG + 2.5 × (4.0 − albumin in g/dL); albumin-corrected delta ratio = (albumin-corrected AG − 12)/(24 − HCO3).
Model Reasoning: Only pretreatment admission values are used. For these monovalent ions, 1 mEq/L = 1 mmol/L, so their numerical concentrations are unchanged. Albumin is already in the required g/dL units; no conversion is needed. The standard albumin correction adds 2.5 mEq/L per 1 g/dL that albumin is below 4.0. AG = 142.8 − (125.5 + 7.5) = 9.8 mEq/L. Albumin-corrected AG = 9.8 + 2.5 × (4.0 − 4.2) = 9.3 mEq/L. Delta ratio = (9.3 − 12)/(24 − 7.5) = −2.7/16.5 = −0.1636, rounded to −0.16.
